subject: Limited runbook access + tiered discount for Atlas Health (exec approval)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Mara Singh <mara.singh@atlashealth.com>, Atlas Health Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Atlas pilot — request: limited runbook access + pricing ask

Team — looping you in on Atlas (pilot, potential 18-month commercial). Quick summary: Atlas wants a private deployment inside their Azure tenant (VPC) with an on-site control plane and a short audit window. Security asked for a narrow set of runbook pages and a one-week forensics access window for incident response.

What Atlas is asking: 
- Runbook excerpts (operational steps for failover, patching) shared under NDA, read-only, accessible to two Atlas SecOps users.
- A one-week, timeboxed forensics/export window for debug (only with 48h notice).
- A 20% tiered discount on committed monthly GPUs for the first 6 months in exchange for a 12-month reserved term.

We have product/infra engineering constraints on providing runbook extracts — we can redact internal IPs but can't provide full SOPs. Deal desk patched a term sheet (attached) with a redline that narrows the runbook share to "operational excerpts only" plus a strict attestation & limited access mechanism.

Ask: We need exec signoff to accept the limited runbook access (attestation + 48h approval gating) and approve the 20% introductory discount as a Deal Desk concession. Jordan — can you confirm the margin impact? Karthik — any infra that will block sharing the excerpt? Vanessa — want you to own the exec note and ping Aditya for final signoff.

Attachments: atlas_svc_requirements.pdf, term_sheet_v3.docx

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>, Mara Singh <mara.singh@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Atlas pilot — request: limited runbook access + pricing ask

Aditya — raising to you as requested. TL;DR: Atlas (healthcare SaaS) is close to signing for a 12-month reserved private deployment. They require: limited, read-only access to specific runbook pages (restricted to two Atlas SecOps IDs) and a timeboxed 7-day forensics export window (48h notice). In return they want a 20% discount for first 6 months.

Why this is sensitive:
- Runbook excerpts include operational commands and triage flows — exposing them increases root-cause reproducibility risk. We propose redaction of internal hostnames and removal of product dev notes. Access must be read-only via a secure viewer and logged.
- Forensics export can expose logs; we want a strict data egress process: pre-approval, scoped time window, and an engineer present to supervise.
- Discount is material but within Deal Desk band if we get a 12-month commit and a non-negotiable SLA.

Proposed executive guardrails for approval (recommendation):
1) Approve runbook excerpt sharing limited to: 3 docs, read-only, 2 Atlas accounts, must sign supplemental NDA and a runbook access addendum.
2) Forensics window: 7 days, triggered only for incidents classified Sev1/2, 48h notice, engineer mediation, redacted export where possible.
3) Commercial: 12-month reserved term, 20% discount on committed units for first 6 months only, standard renewal pricing thereafter.
4) Legal to add an audit clause that Atlas cannot further share runbook content; violation = termination + clawback of discount.

If you approve, I'll send an executive memo to Legal and Aditya for final signoff. Need response by COB tomorrow — Atlas is asking for written confirmation to proceed with onboarding next week.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T13:28:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Atlas pilot — request: limited runbook access + pricing ask

Vanessa / Aditya — quick cost view: if we accept 20% off for first 6 months on their committed baseline (anticipated 8 GPUs reserved), initial margin is compressed but still positive — estimated net gross margin ~26% after infra and support allocation. The revenue upsell potential (multi-region rollouts) and 12-month commitment make this within acceptable risk tolerance for sales-led ARR.

Operational risk: we need Karthik to confirm that we can implement access logs and read-only viewer for exactly two external IDs before we sign. If not, the fallback is a redacted PDF snapshot delivered through a monitored SFTP for a one-time review (less ideal for the customer).

If Aditya is comfortable with the legal guardrails Vanessa suggested, Deal Desk signs off on the discount.

— Jordan
Senior Deal Desk Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Fwd: Atlas pilot — request: limited runbook access + pricing ask — Executive OK

Team — after reviewing Legal's redlines and engineering notes from Karthik, I approve the proposed guardrails with one additional condition: any runbook access must be mediated through a temporary, audit-logged viewer we control (no static exports to Atlas). Forensics export is allowed one time per incident, only after a written authorization from our Security lead and with an engineer present to remove sensitive fields.

Commercially: Approved the 20% introductory discount for first 6 months against a 12-month committed reservation amount. Finance to issue a one-time clawback clause for any breach of the runbook-sharing addendum. Jordan — reflect the clawback language in the final term sheet and route to DocuSign. Vanessa — you can confirm to Atlas that we have executive signoff and request the NDAs for the named SecOps users.

Please keep the runbook extract to the minimum necessary. I am cc'ing Legal via Ben's thread to finalize the addendum.

Aditya Rao
VP, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
